newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PM sees 96/97 GDP growth at 6.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: India's PM sees 96/97 GDP growth at 6.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was quoted on Tuesday as saying the country's gross domestic product (GDP) was expected to grow 6.5 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) over the previous fiscal year.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Deve Gowda as telling economists and industrialists in New Delhi that industrial production was forecast to increase by eight percent in 1996/97 over the previous year.

The latest 1996/97 GDP growth estimate given by Deve Gowda was unchanged from the government's previous official target of 6.5 percent growth. GDP grew 6.6 percent in 1995/96 over the previous fiscal year.

Deve Gowda was quoted as saying that over the medium term, the government was committed to a target of seven percent annual economic growth as set in a policy blueprint unveiled by his centre-left coalition government when it assumed office in June.

Business leaders last week told Reuters that industrial production was expected to grow by eight percent in 1996/97 against an official target of 12 percent. Industry output expanded by 12.1 percent in 1995/96.
"The meeting with the prime minister was very productive," economist Raja Chelliah told reporters after the closed-door meeting.
PTI quoted Deve Gowda as saying that his coalition government assumed office "under an economic environment (which) had some inherent weakness".
"The government has boldly faced these inherent disadvantages," Deve Gowda was quoted as saying.
